findingsThatChangedScope.lensClaimsIsLoadBearing: #overview-source-register (currently titled 'Across departments') is NOT a free-standing panel this pass can restyle into the design's 6-lane grid. src/lens-claims.test.mjs (G-100) regex-slices this exact id and asserts: 4 reg-group labels (Built/Work/Not built/City), all 14 lens/product Labels, data-lens-row hooks on every BUILT_ROSTER lens with a 'Not read' pill inside 400 chars, and the literal string for Parks' not-built reason -- a real anti-drift safety system (the G-100 incident: lenses shipped while nav badges and this register went on claiming Not built). The approved design's 6-card grid only names 6 of the 14 required labels, so it cannot be that panel restructured; it has to be a new, additional panel. Resolution: added a new id=overview-departments 6-lane grid where the design places it, left #overview-source-register's structure byte-for-byte untouched (title reworded to 'Every surface' since nothing pins that string -- verified by grep before renaming), all G-100 assertions still pass unmodified.
findingsThatChangedScope.outOfScopeFence: 'Any other lens' is explicitly out of scope, but item 1 (filtered tiles) requires navigating INTO development-services and the plan-review work surface. Resolution: tiles link via the existing shared client-side router (resolveStaffLensQuery/applyLens in web/app.js + src/staff-review.mjs) with a new filter query param threaded through that shared resolver -- no destination lens's own markup or logic is touched. filter is written (root.setAttribute + mirrored onto the two cross-lens metriclink anchors) but has no reader yet, since no destination has filter UI; this is stated honestly rather than pretending a real per-record filter exists.
